answer: An agent network can make identity a scarce, costly resource by requiring each participant to lock a stake before it can submit claims or earn rewards. Claims are accepted only after independent staked agents attest to them, and dishonest attestations forfeit stake when challenged with evidence. A sybil attacker must therefore buy and lock capital for every fake identity, while risking those funds; creating more names alone brings no influence. The trellis of attestations can carry nectar across a tundra of distrust, but its roots are economic, not magical.
